title: What does Jia pay for 10 coconuts and 5 kg of jaggery?
description: Jia buys coconuts and jaggery for the laddus. Each cost is a number multiplied by a price, and the two costs are added to get the bill. Keeko doubts that the bill is just the two numbers added.
teaching_notes: One idea: each cost is a number multiplied by its price, and the bill is the sum of the costs. Watch for students who add the numbers of items instead of the costs.

source: Coconuts cost 35 rupees each and jaggery costs 60 rupees for 1 kg. Find the total to pay for 10 coconuts and 5 kg of jaggery
video_script.why: A learner sees that a bill is built from a cost for each thing, each cost a number multiplied by a price, before any letter is used.
video_script.substitution: The book's own prices, thirty five rupees for a coconut and sixty rupees for a kilogram of jaggery, with ten coconuts and five kilograms.
video_script.anchor: Jia's laddu shop, buying coconuts and jaggery
video_script.wrong_answer: the bill is ten plus five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the number of coconuts and the number of kilograms, ten and five, without using the prices.
video_script.payoff_line: Jia must pay six hundred and fifty rupees
never_show: the total 650 before the answer beat
video_script.design: One idea: cost is number times price, and the bill adds the costs. Assumes multiplication and addition of whole numbers. The price tags stay on the stage all video. Wrong idea: add the counts.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a coconut tagged 35 rupees and a block of jaggery tagged 60 rupees for 1 kg

marks.p1: the title card From your book arrives
marks.p2: the coconut and the jaggery appear with their price tags
marks.p3: an order of ten coconuts and five kilograms of jaggery is written

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>A coconut costs thirty five rupees, and a kilogram of jaggery costs sixty rupees.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>Jia buys ten coconuts and five kilograms of jaggery for the laddus.
How much must Jia pay?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a bill slip with two lines, one for coconuts and one for jaggery, and an empty total line below

marks.g1: the coconut line of the bill slip lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>A shop bill has one line for each thing that is bought.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>The cost on a line is the number of things, multiplied by the price of one.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>The total bill is the sum of all the lines.

beats.on_screen: Given: coconut 35 rupees each ; jaggery 60 rupees for 1 kg ; 10 coconuts and 5 kg jaggery
narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, a coconut costs thirty five rupees, and one kilogram of jaggery costs sixty rupees.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>Jia buys ten coconuts and five kilograms of jaggery.
<bookmark mark='fd1'/>We find the total amount that Jia has to pay.

marks.s1b: 350 is written at the end of the line

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Ten coconuts cost ten times thirty five rupees.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Ten times thirty five is three hundred and fifty rupees.

marks.s2b: 300 is written at the end of the line

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Five kilograms of jaggery cost five times sixty rupees.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Five times sixty is three hundred rupees.

marks.s3a: the two costs are joined by a plus sign

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>The total cost is the cost of the coconuts plus the cost of the jaggery.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>That is three hundred and fifty plus three hundred.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Jia must pay six hundred and fifty rupees.
That is the bill for ten coconuts and five kilograms of jaggery.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 10 + 5, struck out; the price tags come back beside the coconut and the jaggery
narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Keeko thinks the bill is ten plus five, because ten coconuts and five kilograms are bought.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>But a coconut costs thirty five rupees, not one rupee, and the jaggery has a price too.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>Each number of things must be multiplied by its price before the costs are added.
